_comment: Benchmarks the nightly job must report (T-1801), checked by tools/benchmark/compare_benchmarks.py --required. Keys are className.testName; each listed metric prefix must match at least one reported metric. A benchmark that is intentionally not run by the job goes under optional with its reason. A result that is neither required nor optional fails the gate, so a renamed test cannot slip through. The listed metrics are the ones a GitHub-hosted emulator reports: it has no SurfaceFlinger frame timeline, so FrameTimingMetric yields frameCount alone and the jank metrics frameDurationCpuMs and frameOverrunMs of plan §9 need a physical device (ADR-0018 addendum).

control._comment: Runner-health control (T-1801). These microbenchmarks time fixed synthetic drawing and mask computation in process, with no UI, no frame timeline and no dataset, so a change to the app's screens or data cannot move them. When they move far, the machine moved: both degraded nightly runs blew them up while the code that draws them was byte-identical to the baseline commit (run 35953669737 sunArcBitmap +348.8 %, progressRingBitmap +241.3 %; run 36040359691 progressRingBitmap +258.4 %, moonBitmap +75.6 %). A control outside its band makes the whole comparison inconclusive rather than failed, because timings from that machine cannot be trusted. Editing the code one of these benchmarks draws means its baseline must be re-recorded, as for any benchmark. GlanceWidgetBenchmark.emptyBaseline composes a widget that draws nothing, so it times GlanceAppWidget.compose itself; a widget's own composition cost is its figure minus this one (2026-10-07: the four widgets sat within 2.5 % of each other at ~410 ms on both a phone and a hosted emulator, which is a harness floor, not content).
